body: @peilii can these types of fixes go directly to `main` and cherry pick into necessary branch after?

> _Review generated with AI assistance_

Reviewed locally at `715f5ef` against merge-base `4dcdeca02`.

## Blocking

**1. Branch does not compile.** `cargo check -p dynamo-llm --lib`:

```
lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2778:85  E0308: expected `&str`, found `&ChatCompletionMessageContent`
lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2838:66  E0599: no method named `len` on `&ChatCompletionMessageContent`
lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2865:65  E0308: expected `ChatCompletionMessageContent`, found `String`
```

`delta.content` is `Option<ChatCompletionMessageContent>`, an enum of `Text(String) | Parts(Vec<...>)` (`dynamo-protocols/src/types/chat.rs:488`). This is a design question rather than three casts: the recovery scheme assumes flat `String` content it can byte-count and slice, so the `Parts` variant needs an explicit decision. Matches CI — `rust-tests (.)` and `rust-clippy (.)` are red.

Also `prompt.rs:62`: `warning: unused doc comment` — a `///` comment cannot attach to a `thread_local!` macro invocation. Use `//` or move it inside. This alone fails clippy under `-D warnings`.

**2. `cargo fmt --check` fails in four places**: `prompt.rs:129`, `preprocessor.rs:77`, `preprocessor.rs:2775`, and a stray blank line added at `chat_completions.rs:128` that looks like an unrelated edit artifact.

**3. The renderer already performs this normalization on this exact path.** GLM-5.2's standalone `chat_template.jinja` is read into `config.chat_template` at `prompt.rs:335` and handed to `PromptFormatter::from_parts` — the same `HfTokenizerConfigJsonFormatter` whose `render()` already calls `normalize_tool_calls_arguments_in_messages()` (`dynamo-renderer/src/template/oai.rs:500`), gated on whether the template contains `arguments is string`.

That leaves two cases, and it would help to know which one you are hitting:
- The template has no `arguments is string`, the renderer normalizes already, and `detect_tool_arguments_mode` adds a second no-op pass.
- The template does contain it, the renderer is skipping deliberately, and this change silently overrides that opt-out. Per `dynamo-renderer/src/template.rs:109-120` the reason for the opt-out is that pre-parsing forces the `tojson` branch and re-emits with minijinja's compact separators, breaking append-only prefix matching across multi-step tool-use turns — the same ISL/prefix-reuse parity this PR is chasing.

Either way the detection belongs in dynamo-renderer next to the existing `template_handles_args_string`, not as a parallel mechanism in `messages()`. A rendered-prompt dump for a two-turn tool-use conversation would settle it.

**4. Speculative prefill renders with a different mode, producing a prefix mismatch.** `speculative_prefill.rs:155` calls `formatter.render(&prefill_request)` with no `ToolArgumentsModeGuard`, from a spawned background task, and `SpeculativePrefillRequest::messages()` (`speculative_prefill.rs:54`) never normalizes. So for GLM-5.2 the speculative path renders `arguments` as a JSON string while the main path renders it as an object. The warmed KV prefix will not match the real next-turn request, defeating speculative prefill precisely on tool-use turns — the same class of failure this PR is trying to fix.

**5. The vLLM/SGLang parity decision is overridden unconditionally.** `dynamo-parsers/src/tool_calling/parsers.rs:186-189`: "GLM-4.7 intentionally omitted: match upstream vLLM/SGLang behavior (drop the call when `</tool_call>` is missing)." Every glm47 deployment flips to TRT-LLM behavior, hardcoded on parser name, with no flag and no update to that comment. The new code comments acknowledge the markup leak, which is an improvement, but acknowledging it is not the same as making it opt-in.

## Design

**6. The thread-local is a hidden global for what is a per-request parameter.** `RENDER_TOOL_ARGUMENTS_MODE` (`prompt.rs:65`) couples `OpenAIPreprocessor` to `OAIChatLikeRequest::messages()` with no compile-time link. The guard at `preprocessor.rs:876` is correct today — `apply_template` is sync and nothing awaits inside the block — but that correctness rests on a comment, and finding 4 is the failure mode already present in-tree. The stated reason for avoiding a struct field (updating every struct literal) does not apply if the detection lives in the renderer, where the formatter already owns per-template flags.

**7. `detect_tool_arguments_mode` is a narrow substring match with a silent-miss gap.** `prompt.rs:53` matches only `_args.items()` and `arguments.items()`; the minijinja filter form (`arguments | items`, used in dynamo-renderer's own test at `oai.rs:1591`) does not match. And `mdc_jinja_template_text` (`prompt.rs:101`) returns `None` when the template is embedded in `tokenizer_config.json` rather than a standalone `.jinja`, so the fix silently does not apply to those deployments.

**8. Streaming and non-streaming now do opposite things on the same event.** Streaming (`preprocessor.rs:2831`) emits the raw `<tool_call>` markup as content for TRT-LLM parity; non-streaming (`aggregator.rs:422`) sets `choice.text = String::new()`. The same truncated turn yields markup with `stream=true` and an empty turn with `stream=false`.

The aggregator arm is also a behavior change relative to base, in the opposite direction from the PR's stated goal: before this PR the arm did not exist and `choice.text` retained the raw text; now it is wiped. If dropping is the intended non-streaming semantic, that deserves its own callout in the description rather than arriving inside a parity fix.

## Correctness

**9. Recovery chunk is emitted before its own chunk.** `preprocessor.rs:2878-2881` pushes `recovery` ahead of `nv_chunk`. The jail's `finalize()` emission can carry both the pre-marker prose and `finish_reason` in one chunk (jail entered mid-chunk, prose in `accumulated_content`), so the client receives `<tool_call>...` before the prose that preceded it. Appending `dropped` to the triggering choice's own `delta.content` on that chunk is order-safe and removes the clone/retain/usage-clearing entirely.

**10. The byte-offset heuristic is fragile.** `input_text[emitted_content_len..]` assumes emitted content is a verbatim prefix of jail input. The finalize path `trim_end()`s the prefix, and any path moving text into `reasoning_content` desyncs the offset. `.get(..).unwrap_or("")` prevents the panic but yields wrong text rather than nothing, so a garbled mid-word slice reaches the client. Locating the first `<tool_call>` in `input_text` and emitting from there is more robust.

## Testing

**11. No tests**, across 238 added lines. `lib/llm/tests/test_streaming_tool_parsers.rs` already drives `apply_tool_calling_jail` directly. Suggested minimum: truncated block recovered; complete block not recovered; n=2 with one truncated choice; non-glm47 parser is a no-op; `detect_tool_arguments_mode` over both the GLM-5.2 template and the `| items` filter form; and a two-turn render asserting the prompt prefix is stable.

## Minor

- Both new log messages contain a long run of embedded spaces from a wrapped string literal (`preprocessor.rs:2849`, `aggregator.rs:435`) and will render that way in logs.
- `ToolArgumentsMode`, `detect_tool_arguments_mode`, and `mdc_jinja_template_text` are `pub`, adding public API surface for what are internal helpers. `pub(crate)` matches the rest of the module.
- `normalize_tool_call_arguments` does `tc.pointer("/function/arguments")` and then re-fetches `tc.get_mut("function")` — two lookups where the renderer's equivalent does one.

Closing as superseded by the fixes merged into main:

- https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/12332 — tool-call argument normalization (merged August 11, 2026).
- https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/12333 — truncated tool-call recovery (merged August 10, 2026).
